questions.q: What does Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution state about the Council of Ministers?
questions.a: Article 75(3) states: "The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha)." A wrong answer (e.g., saying responsible to the President or Rajya Sabha) reveals a misunderstanding of the foundational accountability mechanism in India's parliamentary system.

questions.q: Why is collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha considered the cornerstone of parliamentary democracy in India?
questions.a: Collective responsibility ensures that the executive (Council of Ministers) remains accountable to the directly elected representatives of the people (Lok Sabha). It forces the government to maintain majority support, making it responsive to public opinion. A wrong answer that focuses only on the Prime Minister's power or the President's role shows confusion between parliamentary and presidential systems.

questions.q: In a coalition government, if one coalition partner withdraws support and the government loses a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha, what happens to the Council of Ministers? Explain using the principle of collective responsibility.
questions.a: The entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign because collective responsibility means they stand or fall together. The loss of confidence by the Lok Sabha applies to the whole ministry, not just the withdrawing partner. A wrong answer suggesting only the withdrawing partner's ministers resign indicates a failure to grasp the "collective" nature of the responsibility.

questions.q: Compare the accountability of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha with the accountability of the US President to the Congress. What structural difference in the executive-legislature relationship does this reveal?
questions.a: In India, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and can be removed by a no-confidence motion; in the US, the President is not responsible to Congress and cannot be removed by a legislative vote (only by impeachment for high crimes). This reveals the fusion of powers in parliamentary systems versus separation of powers in presidential systems. A wrong answer that claims both are similar shows inability to distinguish executive-legislature relations across systems.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha makes the Indian Prime Minister more powerful than the US President because the PM controls a guaranteed legislative majority." Is this a valid assessment? Justify.
questions.a: The statement is partially valid but oversimplified. While the PM usually commands a majority, collective responsibility also makes the PM vulnerable to coalition pressures and party dissent; the US President has fixed tenure and independent legislative powers. A valid evaluation must weigh both the advantage of majority support and the constraint of continuous accountability. A wrong answer that simply agrees or disagrees without nuance shows lack of evaluative depth.

questions.q: Draft a hypothetical constitutional amendment that would replace collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha with individual ministerial responsibility to the Prime Minister. What would be two major consequences for Indian democracy?
questions.a: A good answer would propose an amendment to Article 75(3) making ministers individually responsible to the PM, and identify consequences: (1) erosion of parliamentary accountability as ministers would not need Lok Sabha confidence, (2) strengthening of prime ministerial dominance, potentially leading to authoritarian tendencies. A poor answer would miss the shift in accountability from legislature to executive.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha?
questions.a: Students often think collective responsibility means all ministers must agree on every policy publicly, and that a minister who disagrees must resign immediately.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can explain the meaning of collective responsibility, distinguish it from individual ministerial responsibility, and analyze how a no-confidence motion operates to enforce accountability in a parliamentary system.
